# Atlantic (01, engineer) — SPD-044

## Brief
Objective: Law 7 must hold when git runs a write verb under an alias the git call itself defines. Today git_verb in bin/spud_ledger.py skips `-c` and its value and reads the next word as the verb, and git_refused checks that word against GIT_WRITE_VERBS. git expands an alias before running it, so `git -c alias.p=push p` (and `git -c alias.p='!git push' p`, a shell alias) pushes, while the hook reads verb `p` and refuses nothing. Close every way a single command line can hand git an alias the hook does not read:

- `-c alias.NAME=VALUE` and `-calias.NAME=VALUE` if git accepts the joined form; `--config-env alias.NAME=ENVVAR` and `--config-env=alias.NAME=ENVVAR`.
- Environment config on the same line or exported earlier in it: `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT` with `GIT_CONFIG_KEY_n`/`GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_n`, `GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS`, and `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL`, `GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM` or `GIT_CONFIG` pointing git at a file; through `env`, `export`, a prefix assignment, and inside `sh -c`/`bash -c`/`zsh -c`, `eval` and subshell strings.
- Indirect definitions: `-c include.path=FILE` and `-c includeIf.*.path=FILE`, which load a file that can define aliases.
- Alias values: a value naming a write verb (with or without options, e.g. `alias.p=push --force`), a value naming another alias, and a `!` shell alias whose command is a git write or anything else.

Recommended fix, yours to confirm by probing: for a member (a caller with an agent_id), refuse a git call whose own line defines any alias.*, include.* or includeIf.* key by -c or --config-env, or sets any GIT_CONFIG_* variable listed above, as an unresolvable verb, the way SPD-041 refuses an unresolvable glob. If resolving instead (reading the alias value as the verb, and a `!` value as a shell command fed back through analyse_command) is simple and exact, it may be done, but a key the hook cannot resolve still refuses. Spud (no agent_id) is not held by Law 7 and must see no change. Keep `git -c user.name=x log`, `git -c color.ui=never status`, `git -c core.pager=cat diff` and similar non-alias config silent for members, and add those as controls. The glob readings SPD-041 added (a glob in `-c`'s value or key, `alias.p?=push`, `-c alias.{p,q}=push`) must still be read.

Work red first (superpowers TDD): probe in the scratchpad against a throwaway repository (`git init` in the scratchpad, never this repository or its remote) that each form really expands the alias and runs the verb, using read-only or scratch-repo-local verbs as the stand-in (for example `alias.v=version`, `alias.s=status`, or `alias.c=commit --allow-empty -m x` in the scratch repo) and never `push`. Add a test class to tests/test_hooks.py whose cases fail on the unchanged code, then fix. If you find a related hole outside this brief, probe it and file a proposal rather than fixing it; candidates are aliases in a config file a member could write (a repository's .git/config reached with `-C` or `--git-dir`, or `~/.gitconfig`; none are configured today) and `-c core.hooksPath` or `-c core.sshCommand` running a program.

Done when: the new test class is red on the unchanged code and green after; the full suite passes (`python3.14 -I -S -m unittest discover -s tests -t tests`, run it in the background, about three and a half minutes; report the new count, 522 today); a before/after differential of analyse_command over the existing test command strings loses no finding and changes only lines that define git config; PreToolUse(Bash) latency stays within a millisecond of today's.

Deliverables: bin/spud_ledger.py and tests/test_hooks.py only. Read first: ledger/tickets/SPD-044.md; git_verb, git_refused, GIT_GLOBAL_VALUE_FLAGS and the git branch of analyse_segment (the `git_verb(words)` call) in bin/spud_ledger.py; the Result sections of ledger/teams/SPUD-041/Roseval.md and ledger/teams/SPUD-040/Bintje.md for how globs, env assignments and shell strings are read today.

## Ticket proposals
- **Bash hook: -c core.sshCommand / core.hooksPath run an arbitrary program under an allowed git read verb, bypassing Law 7** — suggested P2; created as [[SPD-046]] at P1 by Spud.
  Why: SPD-044 closed git aliases and GIT_CONFIG_* injection, but git config that names a program to run (core.sshCommand, core.hooksPath, and GIT_SSH_COMMAND) is a different hole: a member's git call can execute an arbitrary command the hook never analyses, under a verb Law 7 allows. git -c core.sshCommand=<cmd> fetch <ssh-remote> runs <cmd> for the ssh transport; fetch/ls-remote/clone are not write verbs, so the hook lets them through. The harness's worktree guard refuses -c core.sshcommand, but Law 7's hook runs in every session (a member sharing the main checkout has no worktree guard), so the Spud hook should refuse a member's git call that sets core.sshCommand/core.hooksPath (by -c/--config-env) or GIT_SSH_COMMAND/GIT_SSH (by env), the same way it now refuses aliases.
  Evidence: Probe: the harness worktree guard itself refuses 'git -c core.sshcommand=... var -l' as config injection whose write effect it cannot verify (SPD-044 scratchpad), confirming git honours it. git docs: core.sshCommand replaces ssh for ssh transport; core.hooksPath relocates hooks. Not fixed here: out of SPD-044's brief, which named it a proposal candidate. bin/spud_ledger.py git_line_defines_alias only refuses sections alias/include/includeIf; core.* is left silent by design.
- **Bash hook: a git alias in a config file reached with -C <repo>, --git-dir, or ~/.gitconfig runs a write verb the hook cannot read** — suggested P3; created as [[SPD-047]] at P2 by Spud.
  Why: SPD-044 refuses -c/--config-env and env config injection, but git also reads aliases from config files the hook does not open: another repository's .git/config reached with 'git -C <repo>' or '--git-dir <dir>', the user's ~/.gitconfig, or a file a GIT_CONFIG* var points at (SPD-044 refuses the file-pointer vars for members, but the .git/config of a repo reached by -C is not covered). A member who can write such a file could define 'alias.p = push' there and then run 'git -C <repo> p'. None are configured today (git config --get-regexp alias. is empty and ~/.gitconfig has no aliases), so this is latent, but the hook has no way to read an on-disk alias table.
  Evidence: git honours [alias] in any config file it loads; probed at SPD-044 that a GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL file with [alias] v=version makes 'git v' run version. The -C/--git-dir cases were not probed (they need a second repo). Writing another repo's .git/config or ~/.gitconfig is normally outside a member's deliverables (the edit hook refuses it), which limits reach. Out of SPD-044's brief, which named it a proposal candidate.
